clue.text: Like a dunce cap Charlie is given after trick with iodine

indicators.note: Charlie is placed after the other pieces, at the end of the answer

parts.note: to con is to trick or swindle
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A description of a dunce's hat, assembled by a trickster with a dose of iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce cap is a tall pointed cone, so it is cone-shaped in form.

clue.text: Emerge and enter golf tournament?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reveal oneself, step out of hiding
second meaning, whimsical: to ..., the British golf championship

explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's oldest major championship, held in Britain; the question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for stepping out of hiding, and read literally means joining golf's Open Championship.

clue.text: Two possible directions from Trondheim, perhaps

parts.note: the first of the two compass directions, north
or marks the choice between two possible alternatives
the second compass direction, south-east

explanation.surface: A traveller ponders which way to head out of a Norwegian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a route question about a city, but the three opening words work as one phrase: a pair of compass points joined by the word for an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Trondheim is a city in Norway, and anything Norwegian is Norse; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Bird grabs the lady's cigar

indicators.note: grabbing holds something within, so the bird goes around the lady's word

parts.note: a coot is a water bird
her means belonging to the lady

explanation.surface: A bird snatches a woman's cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, open at each end.

clue.text: A spot to get drunk with grub?

definitions.text: A spot to get drunk with grub?

indicators.note: being drunk means being scrambled and unsteady, so the letters of the preceding and following words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A pub that serves food is described as a place to drink while eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A SPOT and GRUB are rearranged together, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a pub where you drink and eat good food.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a public house specialising in quality meals as well as beer.

clue.text: Liquor — almost overindulge when upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to gorge is to eat to excess

explanation.surface: Someone nearly drinks too much spirits and feels upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GORGE to GORG, and 'when upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Grog is rum diluted with water, once a sailor's ration, and loosely any alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Cleared out messy desk to confuse daughter

indicators.note: a messy desk is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: to addle is to muddle or confuse
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone fled, leaving a chaotic desk to bewilder their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddled is informal for ran away in a hurry, as one does on clearing off.

clue.text: After a break, begins summaries

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., picks up again after a pause
second meaning: résumés, short summaries or CVs

explanation.walkthrough: The accents of résumés are dropped in the grid, so the verb and the noun share the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means restarts after an interruption, and the noun means brief outlines or synopses.

clue.text: Drink bottles beginning to affect party game

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the drink goes around the next letter

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word, its first letter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A drink starts to take effect at a party where games are played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party game' reads as one phrase, but 'party' gives BALL and only 'game' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat game in which players shoot each other with pellets of dye.

clue.text: Hairdresser covers PC's toupee clumsily — that's controversial in Sydney!

indicators.note: covering goes over and around, so the hairdresser surrounds the jumbled letters

parts.note: a barber is a men's hairdresser

indicators.note: something done clumsily is done badly, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A barber clumsily fits a policeman's wig, causing an uproar in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Australian slang: the hot topic that stops the talk at a barbecue. PC is a police constable, and its 's gives an S to the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a barbecue stopper is a hot topic of debate, one that halts conversation at a social gathering.

clue.text: Dashes to represent Tom in this?

definitions.text: Dashes to represent Tom in this?

parts.words: Dashes to represent Tom in this?
parts.note: T is one dash, O three dashes and M two dashes in the dot-and-dash telegraph alphabet, so the name is spelt with dashes alone

explanation.surface: Someone asks which writing system renders a name called Tom purely as dashes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Morse, T is -, O is --- and M is --, so TOM is written entirely in dashes with no dots.
explanation.definitionFit: The telegraphic alphabet of dots and dashes devised by Samuel Morse renders each letter as a signal pattern.

clue.text: Gym class skipped by more irritating sportsperson

indicators.note: a class that is skipped is missed out, so these letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: peskier means more annoying or irritating
PE is physical education, a school gym class

explanation.surface: A pupil who misses PE is described as even more annoying than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is an athlete who competes on snow slopes, one kind of sportsperson.

clue.text: Not initially pleasant to fight for refrigerator

indicators.note: says the word loses its opening letter, the one it would start with

parts.note: nice means pleasant
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be polite any longer and squares up over a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebox is an older or American word for a fridge, a cold cabinet for keeping food.

clue.text: Leaf pattern in range of colours worn by maiden

indicators.note: something worn by a person is held within them, so the maiden letter sits inside the colour range

parts.note: a palette is the range of colours an artist uses
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A decorative leaf motif comes in a range of colours on a young woman's dress.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmette is an ornamental motif shaped like a fan of palm fronds, used in classical decoration.

clue.text: Drink what in Spanish island?

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail
qué is Spanish for what

explanation.surface: A puzzled drinker on a Spanish island asks for a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French Caribbean island in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Socialist embraces a strange character — The Devil, perhaps

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so the socialist goes around the next letter

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-wing socialist
a card is an eccentric or odd person

explanation.surface: A left-winger hugs an odd person who is a devilish figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Devil is one of the major arcana in a fortune-telling deck; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is one of the trump cards in a fortune-teller's deck, so it is an example.

clue.text: Dog runs home with animated Belgian

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
in means at home
Tintin is the Belgian cartoon reporter created by Hergé

explanation.surface: A dog dashes indoors with a cartoon character from Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Rin Tin Tin was a German Shepherd who starred in Hollywood films of the 1920s.

clue.text: United supporters flipped, creating a big mess

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: U is a common abbreviation for United, as in football team names
fans are supporters

explanation.surface: Football supporters of United flip out, causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAFU is military slang, an acronym for a situation that has gone badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is slang for a chaotic, botched situation or blunder.

clue.text: Ugly cut in garment

indicators.note: something ugly is misshapen, so these letters are put into a different shape

explanation.surface: An unattractive slit has been made in a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose, sleeveless or short-sleeved piece of clothing reaching the hips or knees.

clue.text: Brazilian vehicle, one local uncovered

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: with its covering stripped away, a word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Brazilian man drives a car, one of the area's residents bared.
explanation.definitionFit: A carioca is a native of Rio de Janeiro, so a kind of Brazilian person.

clue.text: Lifts hex mysteriously surrounding European show

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single European letter
something done mysteriously is done in an unaccountable way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A curse is mysteriously lifted around a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysteriously' rearranges LIFTS HEX to THXFILES, and 'surrounding' puts E inside after TH.
explanation.definitionFit: The X-Files is a 1990s American television drama about FBI agents investigating paranormal cases.

clue.text: Refrain from terror when circling globe

indicators.note: circling goes around, so the terror word encloses the globe

parts.note: fear is terror
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from panic as they travel round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back or abstain from doing something.

clue.text: Old record label with award for expatriate

parts.note: EMI was a British record company, now absorbed into others
a grant is a sum of money awarded

explanation.surface: A defunct music label wins an award for a person living abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is someone who has left their home country to settle elsewhere, as an expat has.

clue.text: Quickly typed a letter for dictator?

indicators.note: someone dictating speaks the words aloud, so the phrase is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: pressed, as in pressed a key on a keyboard; O is just one letter of the alphabet, here the one hit

explanation.surface: A secretary is asked how fast a letter was typed for the boss who dictated it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressed O' spoken aloud runs together as the musical tempo word; the dictator is the one saying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction meaning very fast, and it is also used to mean at once.

clue.text: Animal pound

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sea creature with tentacles
second meaning: jocular slang for a quid, a pound sterling

explanation.walkthrough: Squid is a jokey British variant of quid, slang for a pound coin or note.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a ten-armed sea creature and is also humorous British slang for one pound sterling.

clue.text: At first, Jimi Hendrix regularly shown to be forceful character?

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the next word
picking letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: Jimi Hendrix is portrayed as a powerful personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes EDI from HENDRIX. The Force is the mystical energy in Star Wars, hence the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jedi is a Star Wars knight who wields the Force, so a character literally full of it.

clue.text: Garden area essential to occupation

indicators.note: the essential part is the core, so the answer sits in the middle of the following word

explanation.surface: A paved space outside the house is claimed to be vital to someone's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor space next to a house, used for sitting or eating.

clue.text: Signal heard to unexpectedly attack and gain an unfair advantage

indicators.note: says the word is taken by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a cue is a signal to begin, as for an actor
to jump someone is to attack them by surprise

explanation.surface: A signal is heard and someone pounces to get ahead unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue-jump is to push in ahead of people waiting their turn, getting ahead without fair play.

clue.text: I've returned, following female and male relatives to see mountain

indicators.note: the turned-round letters come after the family members, at the end

parts.note: nan is a grandmother, a female relative
dad is a father, a male relative

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I've, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone comes back after visiting their gran and dad to go sightseeing in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatives' serves both 'female' and 'male': nan is a grandmother. The apostrophe in I've is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanda Devi is one of the highest peaks in the Indian Himalayas, in Uttarakhand.

clue.text: Cyclist's condition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who rides a bicycle
second meaning: a clause added to a contract or proviso

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like a cyclist's state of health; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both someone riding a bike and an added stipulation attached to an agreement.
